operations.name: shared_basis
operations.title_en: Statements leaning on the same passage
operations.question_en: Which statements rest on the same textual passage and therefore are not independent?
operations.cypher:
MATCH (e1:Evidence)-[:SUPPORTS]->(c1:Claim), (e2:Evidence)-[:SUPPORTS]->(c2:Claim)
WHERE c1.id IN $claim_ids AND c2.id IN $claim_ids AND c1.id < c2.id
  AND e1.chunk_id = e2.chunk_id
  AND e1.start_char IS NOT NULL AND e2.start_char IS NOT NULL
  AND e1.start_char < e2.end_char AND e2.start_char < e1.end_char
RETURN c1.id AS claim_a, c2.id AS claim_b, e1.id AS ev_a, e2.id AS ev_b,
       e1.chunk_id AS chunk_id, e1.start_char AS a_start, e1.end_char AS a_end,
       e2.start_char AS b_start, e2.end_char AS b_end,
       CASE WHEN e1.id = e2.id THEN 'same_evidence' ELSE 'overlapping_span' END AS relation
ORDER BY claim_a, claim_b
operations.caveat_en: A coarser 'same chunk' test adds a false pair K2/K3 (adjacent, non-overlapping spans [1301,1455) and [1456,1750)). The operation uses span overlap, not chunk identity.
operations.finding_en: {n_rows} pairs of statements rest on the same passage ({anchors}). They support each other less than their number suggests.
operations.finding_empty_en: No pair of statements in this selection shares a textual basis: each one draws on a separate passage.
operations.why_it_matters_en: The argument about Lianzhou draws on a single footnote more than once; counting statements would overstate the evidence.

columns_en.ev_a: Evidence record backing the first statement
columns_en.ev_b: Evidence record backing the second statement
columns_en.a_start: Position of the first statement's quotation inside the source fragment (characters)
columns_en.a_end: End position of the first statement's quotation (characters)
columns_en.b_start: Position of the second statement's quotation inside the source fragment (characters)
columns_en.b_end: End position of the second statement's quotation (characters)
columns_en.relation: same_evidence = both statements cite the very same quotation; overlapping_span = separate but overlapping quotations

operations.name: independent_bases
operations.question_en: How many independent textual bases and how many sources stand behind the slice and behind each feature category?
operations.cypher:
MATCH (c:Claim) WHERE c.id IN $claim_ids
MATCH (c)-[:ABOUT_FEATURE]->(f:Feature)
OPTIONAL MATCH (s:Source)-[:HAS_EVIDENCE]->(e:Evidence)-[:SUPPORTS]->(c)
RETURN f.id AS feature, count(DISTINCT c) AS claims,
       count(DISTINCT e) AS distinct_evidence,
       count(DISTINCT e.chunk_id) AS distinct_chunks,
       count(DISTINCT s) AS distinct_sources,
       collect(DISTINCT s.id) AS source_ids
ORDER BY feature
operations.caveat_en: Every claim in the graph carries exactly one Evidence (checked across the whole active graph on 2026-09-08: 57476/57476). There is no count of independent bases below the claim level; the number is computed per slice after merging shared_basis pairs. Distinct sources are distinct documents, not proven scholarly independence.
operations.finding_en: Across the {n_rows} feature categories in this selection, the {claims_total} statements are backed by {chunks_total} distinct text passages from two source documents.
operations.finding_empty_en: No feature category is present in this selection.
operations.why_it_matters_en: Every claim in the graph carries exactly one evidence record; genuine independence has to be read off distinct passages, which is what this operation counts.

columns_en.feature: Feature category the statements are about
columns_en.claims: Number of statements in this category
columns_en.distinct_evidence: Number of distinct evidence (quotation) records behind them
columns_en.distinct_chunks: Number of distinct text chunks the quotations come from
columns_en.distinct_sources: Number of distinct source documents involved
columns_en.source_ids: Identifiers of the source documents involved

operations.name: source_split
operations.question_en: What does each of the two sources record under each feature category?
operations.cypher:
MATCH (s:Source)-[:HAS_EVIDENCE]->(:Evidence)-[:SUPPORTS]->(c:Claim)
WHERE c.id IN $claim_ids
MATCH (c)-[:ABOUT_FEATURE]->(f:Feature)
RETURN s.id AS document_id, s.title AS source_title, f.id AS feature,
       count(DISTINCT c) AS claims, collect(DISTINCT c.id) AS claim_ids
ORDER BY source_title, feature

operations.name: source_comparison_by_feature
operations.title_en: Are the two sources talking about the same thing?
operations.question_en: In which feature categories do the two sources overlap, and which are unique to one?
operations.cypher:
MATCH (c:Claim)-[:ABOUT_FEATURE]->(f:Feature) WHERE c.id IN $claim_ids
MATCH (s:Source)-[:HAS_EVIDENCE]->(:Evidence)-[:SUPPORTS]->(c)
WITH f.id AS feature,
  sum(CASE WHEN s.id=$source_a AND c.polarity='attested' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS a_att,
  sum(CASE WHEN s.id=$source_a AND c.polarity='not_attested' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS a_nat,
  sum(CASE WHEN s.id=$source_b AND c.polarity='attested' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS b_att,
  sum(CASE WHEN s.id=$source_b AND c.polarity='not_attested' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS b_nat
RETURN feature, a_att, a_nat, b_att, b_nat,
  CASE WHEN (a_att+a_nat)=0 THEN 'unique_b'
       WHEN (b_att+b_nat)=0 THEN 'unique_a'
       WHEN (a_att>0 AND b_nat>0) OR (a_nat>0 AND b_att>0) THEN 'contrast'
       ELSE 'shared' END AS row_class
ORDER BY row_class, feature
operations.caveat_en: The canonical T7 template compares two targets. C2 has a single target (YUE_QINLIAN, 9 of 9 records), so canonical T7 is not executable inside this slice; sources are compared instead. This is free Cypher of the same shape, not the shipped template.
operations.finding_en: Yue-Hashimoto 1991 and Chen & Chen 2005 address the same question in only {shared_count} of the {n_rows} categories recorded here. For the most part they describe different things.
operations.finding_empty_en: No feature category is comparable between these two sources.
operations.why_it_matters_en: Two descriptions filed under one heading are not automatically answers to one question.

columns_en.a_att: Attested-polarity statements from Yue-Hashimoto 1991 in this category
columns_en.a_nat: Not-attested-polarity statements from Yue-Hashimoto 1991 in this category
columns_en.b_att: Attested-polarity statements from Chen–Chen 2005 in this category
columns_en.b_nat: Not-attested-polarity statements from Chen–Chen 2005 in this category
columns_en.row_class: How the two sources relate for this category: shared, unique_a, or unique_b

operations.name: contested_cell
operations.question_en: Is there a feature category where statements about the same target carry opposite polarity?
operations.cypher:
MATCH (c:Claim)-[:ABOUT_FEATURE]->(f:Feature) WHERE c.id IN $claim_ids
MATCH (c)-[:ABOUT_SUBGROUP]->(t:Subgroup)
OPTIONAL MATCH (s:Source)-[:HAS_EVIDENCE]->(:Evidence)-[:SUPPORTS]->(c)
WITH t.id AS target, f.id AS feature,
  sum(CASE WHEN c.polarity='attested' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS att,
  sum(CASE WHEN c.polarity='not_attested' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS nat,
  count(DISTINCT s) AS sources, collect(DISTINCT c.id) AS claim_ids
WHERE att > 0 AND nat > 0
RETURN target, feature, att, nat, sources, claim_ids ORDER BY feature
operations.caveat_en: The single contested cell is a coding artefact, not a scholarly dispute: both claims come from one source and both carry value.present=false. Show it only together with polarity_value_consistency.
operations.finding_en: One pair of statements about voiced obstruents carries opposite signs ({anchors}). Read against their quotations, this is an inconsistency in how the records were coded, not a disagreement between scholars.
operations.finding_empty_en: No two statements here contradict each other outright.
operations.why_it_matters_en: A contradiction in the records is not yet a contradiction in the literature.

columns_en.target: Working address the contested statements are about

operations.name: polarity_value_consistency
operations.question_en: Does the recorded polarity agree with the present flag inside the value?
operations.cypher:
MATCH (c:Claim) WHERE c.id IN $claim_ids
MATCH (c)-[:ABOUT_FEATURE]->(f:Feature)
RETURN c.id AS claim_id, f.id AS feature, c.polarity AS polarity,
  CASE WHEN c.value CONTAINS '"present": true' OR c.value CONTAINS '"present":true' THEN 'present_true'
       WHEN c.value CONTAINS '"present": false' OR c.value CONTAINS '"present":false' THEN 'present_false'
       ELSE 'no_present_flag' END AS present_flag
ORDER BY feature, claim_id
operations.finding_en: Across the {n_rows} statements in this selection, {present_false} carry a present:false flag in their own recorded value; two of those disagree with each other only in polarity, which is exactly the contested cell above, not a genuine dispute about the phonology.
operations.finding_empty_en: No statement is present in this selection.
operations.why_it_matters_en: This is the native explanation for the single contested cell: both disputing statements come from the same source and carry the same present:false value, so the polarity disagreement is a labelling artefact, not a scholarly one.

columns_en.present_flag: Whether the record's own value carries a present:true/false flag

operations.name: feature_level_split
operations.question_en: Does CONS_VOICED_OBSTRUENTS_REPORTED separate a synchronic from a diachronic reading?
operations.cypher:
MATCH (c:Claim)-[:ABOUT_FEATURE]->(:Feature {id:$feature})
MATCH (c)-[:ABOUT_SUBGROUP]->(:Subgroup {id:$target})
WHERE c.status IN $statuses
OPTIONAL MATCH (s:Source)-[:HAS_EVIDENCE]->(e:Evidence)-[:SUPPORTS]->(c)
RETURN c.id AS claim_id, c.idiom_tag AS locality, c.polarity AS polarity,
  CASE WHEN c.value CONTAINS '"present": true' THEN 'present_true'
       WHEN c.value CONTAINS '"present": false' THEN 'present_false'
       ELSE 'no_present_flag' END AS present_flag,
  c.value AS value, c.conditions AS conditions, s.id AS document_id
ORDER BY present_flag, claim_id

operations.caveat_en: In this snapshot present=false coincides with the diachronic reflex and present=true with synchronic voiced fricatives, but the coincidence is observed on 15 claims and is not declared anywhere as a contract. The distinguishing information sits in the free text of value.note; polarity does not separate the levels and conditions is filled in irregularly. For CASE_EN the level stays a curated annotation.
